Big fan of this seashell candle 

Hook
Big fan of whatever this vibe is: handcrafted shells, soft lighting, natural materials, and homes feeling more connected to nature again. 

Main point 1: what makes ours different

* each seashell is hand carved and painted
* we developed our own beeswax candle sand after realizing most “natural” candle sands still used synthetic palm-derived ingredients
* ours is made with beeswax, cotton wicks, and pure essential oils
* Vanilla Cashmere is lavender, sandalwood, and vanilla

Main point 2: why this matters right now

* Architectural Digest’s 2026 interior forecast highlighted the shift toward tactile craftsmanship, artisanal finishes, natural materials, and more emotionally grounding spaces
* people are becoming more aware of synthetic fragrance and what they’re actually burning in their homes
* we wanted the candle to not only look natural, but reflect that in the materials and ingredients used too
* the goal was something timeless, warm, and inspired by nature

Closing thought
We’ve always been drawn to spaces that feel warm, organic, and quietly elevated.

Hook
I love when a top feels unique enough to make an outfit interesting, but still easy to wear multiple ways.

https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZTkTnn3LJ/

Hook
The Fold was probably one of the only names that stayed with us from the very beginning.

Main point 1: how the name came together

* my sister and I went through what felt like endless name revisions trying to find something that felt simple, memorable, and strong
* originally we wanted something connected to our family name because our grandfather had a fashion brand
* but once we started navigating trademarks and expanding across categories like jewelry and clothing, we realized the name had to stand on its own more broadly
* even after dozens of iterations, The Fold kept resurfacing

Main point 2: why “The Fold” felt right

* we loved how the name connects back to fabric, movement, and the way quality materials naturally drape and fold
* it also felt reflective of how individual pieces come together to shape an entire collection
* the name felt modern but still timeless, which is exactly how we want the materials and pieces themselves to feel
* simple enough to remember immediately, but still layered with meaning

Closing thought
The Fold felt like a name that could evolve with us while still staying connected to the materials and design philosophy behind the brand.

Hook
My sister and I own a clean body care brand, and lately we’ve been testing a lavender body oil that started somewhere between skincare, body care, and a nightly reset. 

Main point 1: the formula

* the base is sweet almond, sunflower, grapeseed, avocado, and apricot oil
* a lot of body oils rely heavily on mineral oil, generic vegetable oils, or silicone blends because they’re inexpensive, shelf stable, and create quick slip on the skin
* we wanted ours to feel more treatment-focused: oils that actually condition the skin, soften texture, and leave the skin feeling healthier over time instead of just temporarily glossy
* grapeseed and sunflower help the oil absorb more elegantly, while avocado and apricot give it a richer, more nourishing feel
* lavender essential oil was important to us because we wanted the scent to feel calming without synthetic fragrance
* it also works beautifully as a massage oil because of the texture and glide of the formula

Main point 2: why this direction matters right now

* body care is becoming more treatment-focused instead of just basic hydration
* people are paying closer attention to ingredient transparency and recognizable plant oils
* lavender continues to be one of the most researched essential oils in wellness spaces around relaxation and sensory routines
* we also chose glass packaging because we wanted to avoid unnecessary plastic exposure with an oil-based product while making the experience feel more substantial and intentional

Closing thought
We’ve been really drawn to products lately that make everyday routines feel slower, softer, and a little more grounding.
